findings.claim: The correction now says that conversation history, instructions, memory, and tool results never show the assistant project files the learner did not share. That absolute claim is false for agentic coding assistants: file-search and file-read tools can gather project files without the learner naming or pasting each file. It also conflicts with the next teaching step, which says an opened project may bring files into view. This can give learners an unsafe model of what opening a workspace exposes.

evidence.section: Agentic loop; Tools; What Claude can access: Claude Code searches files to gather context, file tools read code, and it can access files in the project directory and subdirectories; users do not need to specify which files to read.

findings.recommendation: Replace the absolute sentence with tool-dependent language: tools may automatically select context or use permitted tools to read files in the opened workspace, so learners must treat workspace scope and exclusions as part of sharing. Update the Markdown/PDF and source receipt with the same claim and official section.
